clue.text: Space for production of about 30 years!

definitions.text: Space for production of about 30 years!

parts.words: Space for production of about 30 years!
parts.note: a gap or space between one batch of offspring and the next, each batch spanning roughly three decades, read as the divide in attitudes between old and young

explanation.surface: A factory floor set aside for a manufacturing run lasting thirty years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Production' suggests manufacturing, but here it is the producing of children, a span of about thirty years; the 'space' is the difference in outlook between parents and offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the difference in values and attitudes separating parents from their children.

clue.text: Sticky place to go up

parts.note: a eucalyptus oozes sticky resin, and to be up one in the idiom is to be in a sticky situation

explanation.surface: A gluey spot that someone is about to climb.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'up a gum tree' means in serious difficulty, so the tree is both literally sticky and a figuratively sticky place to be up.
explanation.definitionFit: Eucalyptus and similar trees exude resin, and the idiom places someone in trouble up one.

clue.text: After nine, there were less than half the vehicles in the old capital

indicators.note: the following piece is placed after the number word in this charade

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: fewer than half of the eight letters of the word vehicles are kept, taken from the front

explanation.surface: Once it was past nine o'clock, fewer than half the cars remained in the old city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less than half the' keeps three of the eight letters of 'vehicles'. Nineveh, near modern Mosul in Iraq, was the capital of ancient Assyria.
explanation.definitionFit: Nineveh was the ancient Assyrian capital on the Tigris.

clue.text: Ronald in court bringing up tips for the waiters

indicators.note: the man's short name is placed inside the abbreviation for court
in a down clue, bringing up means the court abbreviation is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Ron is the short form of the name Ronald

explanation.surface: A man called Ronald stands up in court to argue about gratuities for restaurant staff.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'bringing up' reverses the court abbreviation before 'in' places the name inside. A tronc is a British term for the pool of tips shared among restaurant staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A tronc is the pooled fund of gratuities divided among staff in hotels and restaurants.

clue.text: See sober members on day of victory

annotationWithheld.why: 'See sober members on day of victory': OBSER + VE needs an anagram of 'sober', but no clue word signals one ('members' is no anagram indicator); likely an OCR misread of the indicator, and no source found
annotationWithheld.clue: See sober members on day of victory

clue.text: Remarkable goal Edward exulted over

indicators.note: remarkable read as re-markable, able to be marked out again in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
Ted is a familiar short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Edward scored a remarkable goal and then rubbed it in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remarkable' signals the anagram of GOAL plus TED (a pet form of Edward).
explanation.definitionFit: To gloat is to dwell with smug pleasure on one's own success or another's misfortune.

clue.text: Going up and down in style

definitions.meaning: running vertically, at right angles to the horizontal
the late English Gothic manner of architecture marked by strong vertical lines

explanation.surface: Something rising and falling with flair.
explanation.walkthrough: Perpendicular is the name of the last phase of English Gothic architecture, from the late 14th to the 16th century.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means exactly vertical, and also names an English Gothic building manner of the 1300s to 1500s.

clue.text: Man is back before Monday

indicators.note: the reversed piece comes ahead of the weekday abbreviation
the little word is is written from end to start

explanation.surface: A fellow returns just ahead of the start of the working week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like part of the surface's subject, but it is the definition: any man's first name will do.
explanation.definitionFit: Simon is a man's first name, so a man is a fair general pointer to it.

clue.text: Trip over and come upon something unexpectedly

parts.note: to trip is to stumble
across can mean over, as in across the river

explanation.surface: Someone falls over a thing and so discovers it by chance.
explanation.definitionFit: To find something by chance is to happen on it without looking.

clue.text: Concocts a story before the trip, a wide-ranging superficial examination

indicators.note: the invented-story piece is placed ahead of the journey word

parts.note: to cook up or cook a story is to invent it
a tour is a trip

explanation.surface: Someone invents a tale ahead of a journey, then gives a quick, sweeping review.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cook's tour, named after Thomas Cook's package tours, is a rapid survey that touches on much but looks at nothing in depth.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase comes from Thomas Cook's hurried package holidays and means a brief survey of many things.

clue.text: In company, plays unharmonious song

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit inside the abbreviation for company
lacking harmony, so the letters of plays are out of order

explanation.surface: A theatre troupe stages a discordant piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unharmonious' makes ALYPS, and 'In' puts it inside the firm abbreviation. The surface reads 'plays' as theatre, but it is only the letters to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A calypso is a West Indian ballad form, especially from Trinidad.

clue.text: Sort out a Parisian quintet in real trouble

parts.note: un is the French for a, as a Parisian would say it

indicators.note: the numeral goes inside the rearranged letters
in trouble, so the letters of real are disturbed

parts.note: a quintet is five, the Roman numeral V

explanation.surface: Someone untangles a French group of five musicians caught in genuine difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' makes RAEL, and 'in' places the Roman five inside, giving RAVEL; 'a Parisian' asks for the French article, a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: To unravel a problem is to untangle and resolve it.

clue.text: Surgical instrument cut tree badly!…

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone hacks clumsily at a tree, as though with a surgeon's tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' signals the anagram of CUT TREE.
explanation.definitionFit: A curette is a small scoop-shaped tool used for scraping tissue in medical procedures.

clue.text: … worker finds companion by the tree

indicators.note: the companion abbreviation stands right beside the insect

parts.note: a worker is a sterile female bee, a crossword staple
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: An employee meets a friend beside the tree.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is Companion of Honour, a British award. The clue continues from the previous one, whose tree is the one being cut.
explanation.definitionFit: The beech is a familiar smooth-barked broadleaf species of woodland.

clue.text: Gave a warning that there was no more drink

parts.note: port is a fortified wine from Portugal
something ended is no more

explanation.surface: Someone warned that the bar had run dry.
explanation.walkthrough: Read cryptically, 'no more drink' is PORT ENDED, the pieces swapped into answer order.
explanation.definitionFit: To portend is to foreshadow or signal in advance something coming, often ominous.

clue.text: One taking stock of others

parts.note: stock here is livestock, and taking it from other people is cattle theft, not an inventory check

explanation.surface: An auditor counting up someone else's inventory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking stock' looks like doing an inventory, but it is stealing livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a thief of cattle or horses, especially in the American West.

clue.text: Notorious gorge I use by arrangement

indicators.note: the letters are set out in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone admits to using a canyon by prior booking, scandalously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by arrangement' signals the anagram of GORGE I USE.
explanation.definitionFit: Egregious means outstandingly bad, shocking in a way that is widely known.

clue.text: Honourable theologian taken in by gunners in Welsh valley

indicators.note: the title and degree go inside the artillery abbreviation

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian

explanation.surface: A distinguished clergyman is captured by artillerymen in a Welsh valley.
explanation.walkthrough: RA (Royal Artillery) surrounds HON and DD (Doctor of Divinity). The Rhondda is a former coal-mining valley in South Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhondda is a former coal-mining district of South Wales.

clue.text: Turns and leaves

definitions.meaning: becomes sour or rotten, as milk does

explanation.surface: Someone spins round and walks out.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means spoils, as food does, and also departs.

clue.text: Medicinal note?

definitions.meaning: restorative, invigorating, as a medicine is
the keynote, the first degree of a musical scale

explanation.surface: A remark about medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: In music the tonic is the first note of a scale, the home key.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a restorative medicine and also the keynote of a musical scale.

clue.text: Duty charged on one fellow driver

indicators.note: in a down clue the levy is placed on top of the rest

parts.note: a duty is a tax
I is the Roman numeral one
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A levy is imposed on a single motorist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charged on' puts TAX above I and MAN in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A cab driver is a chauffeur of a hired car, so a driver fits.

clue.text: Worn strip

parts.note: worn here means put on as clothing, and the strip is a band of cloth knotted at the collar

explanation.surface: A frayed length of material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worn' looks like frayed, but it means put on: a strip of cloth that is worn.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a long strip of fabric worn knotted under a shirt collar.

clue.text: Child with new role has a highly infectious disease

indicators.note: a new form of the word role is a rearrangement of it

explanation.surface: A youngster with a fresh part in the play catches a dangerous illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' makes OLER; 'with' and 'has' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Cholera is an acute bacterial infection of the intestine spread by contaminated water.

clue.text: Priest's vestment on an old saint

indicators.note: in a down clue the robe is placed above the little word an

parts.note: an alb is a white linen robe worn by clergy

explanation.surface: A clergyman's robe draped on an ancient holy man.
explanation.walkthrough: St Alban is honoured as the first British Christian martyr.
explanation.definitionFit: Alban was a Roman-era martyr, the first recorded in Britain.

clue.text: Law I state of the words of a language

definitions.text: of the words of a language

parts.note: lex is Latin for law
CAL is an abbreviation for California, a US state

explanation.surface: Someone declares a legal statement about vocabulary.
explanation.walkthrough: LEX is Latin for law; CAL is an abbreviation for California.
explanation.definitionFit: Lexical means relating to vocabulary, the stock of terms in a tongue.

clue.text: Additional Stock Exchange employee, he does casual work

parts.note: odd can mean extra or additional, as in an odd sock or odd change
a jobber was a dealer on the old London Stock Exchange

explanation.surface: A spare stockbroker's clerk takes on occasional work.
explanation.walkthrough: A jobber was a wholesale dealer on the London Stock Exchange before the reforms of 1986.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes on small, occasional tasks for pay is a handyman of piecework.

clue.text: Tom returns by alternative form of transport

indicators.note: the alternative word sits beside the reversed name
the name Tom comes back the other way, read from end to start

parts.note: or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Tom comes back by another means of travel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns TOM into MOT, with OR 'by' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A car is commonly called a motor in Britain, a vehicle for getting about.

clue.text: Way to go in for teaching?

definitions.text: Way to go in for teaching?

parts.words: Way to go in for teaching?
parts.note: to go in for something is usually to take it up as a career, but here it is a literal door used by the people who teach

explanation.surface: A question about how to enter the profession of schoolteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go in for teaching' suggests taking up a career, but it means a door for school employees.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the door reserved for employees, such as the teachers of a school.
